elements.evidence: The rendered clause retains a mutual covenant binding Customer: "Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party who are directly involved in performing the Services..." The drafter deliberately targeted the fallback rather than deleting § 22.14.
Rendered language opens "Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party" — bilateral in both original and redline; no change needed.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Operative text now qualifies the class as employees "who are directly involved in performing the Services", replacing the original blanket "the employees of the other party".

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "during their involvement and for twelve (12) months thereafter" replaces "during the Term of this Agreement"; the temporal anchor is the end of the individual's involvement and the tail is exactly 12 months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The foregoing restriction does not apply to general advertisements..." — an express carve-out from the operative prohibition.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence: "...or to unsolicited approaches by an employee."

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The only verb is "solicit"; no "employ or engage", "hire" or "induce ... to leave" language appears in § 22.14 or elsewhere in the cited text, so no no-hire exists to delete.

reasons: All six fallback elements are met in the rendered operative language: mutuality and solicit-only scope were already present, and the redline supplies the narrowed personnel class, the 12-month-post-involvement anchor, and both carve-outs. The fallback level is position-complete.

Preferred level is not met and is not claimed: a non-solicit continues to bind Customer. That is acceptable under the playbook, which treats a clause sitting at the fallback as the redline target here.

Minimality holds. The edits touch only scope, duration and the carve-out sentence — exactly the three defects identified. The deletion of "for any reason" is not a cosmetic or gratuitous removal: that phrase would directly contradict the required general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, so its removal is necessary to avoid an internally inconsistent retained sentence rather than a free-standing narrowing.
No extras were added: no survival tail, no notice mechanic, no damages or expense language, no duplicate covenant, and the carve-out is a single sentence tied to "the foregoing restriction".

Intent is preserved. The clause keeps its heading, numbering and bilateral direction; "Services" and "Term" usage leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference (the Term reference was replaced, not orphaned), and nothing elsewhere in the Agreement is contradicted since § 22.14 is the sole solicitation covenant.
Deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, carve-out present, both operations applying, coverage and minimality gates) were inspected in substance and match the rendered text.
